Hi Neha / Jordan —

Thanks for the call this morning. We're ready to move forward but need a clean sequencing for the paperwork so our procurement team can complete the PO and signature path. A couple of asks from our side:

- Can Redwood consolidate Exhibit B (capacity/throughput schedule) into a single exhibit instead of multiple stacked exhibits? Our legal prefers a single canonical table.
- We need explicit wording on phasing: if we ramp by quarters, how do credits / pro-rates apply?
- Sasha from legal had redlines around the SLA credit definition when capacity falls below the guaranteed baseline.

I've attached a small summary and our internal procurement checklist. Ideally we close paperwork by end of next week.

Sanjay

Appreciate the clarity. Short answers up-front: yes, we can consolidate Exhibit B into a single schedule; pro-ration model is standard and we can add explicit examples; SLA credit language can be tightened — I'll loop in Legal to take the redline.

2) Marcus will draft a revised SLA-credit clause that ties credits to measurable baseline and cadence.
3) We'll circulate a redline to Sasha by EOD tomorrow so your legal team has time to review before Friday.

Can you confirm the signers (name + title) and preferred DocuSign routing? That will help Laura pre-configure the sign path.

Thanks — aiming to keep timeline tight so ops can push PO.

Thanks for the quick turnaround. A few legal points from my side after an initial pass of the redline:

1) Exhibit consolidation: acceptable, but please add a short preamble that ties the single exhibit to the Order Form by version/date to avoid confusion during future amendments.
2) SLA-credit trigger: we need the measurement method to be explicitly defined (metric name + aggregation/rollup). The proposed "5-minute average over one business hour" is fine but call out which monitoring endpoint or metric we will reference (e.g., "platform_token_throughput" or equivalent).
3) Indemnity/tax clause: small language clash in Section 7 — I'll send a marked suggestion separately.

If you can incorporate the preamble and the metric reference, we can greenlight the DocuSign routing. Otherwise we'll request one more iteration.

Sasha Li
Senior Counsel, ClearCrest
